# Implementation Plan: Port the crews progress-bg Stop-hook gate to CODEX members
<!-- ralph-meta {"overviewTaskId":"crews-codex-progress-bg-gate-stall-detection"} -->


*Generated by `/plan-with-ralph` on 2026-06-10. Ready for `/implement-with-ralph --from-plan <job_dir>/plan.md`.*

## Overview

The crews plugin's Stop-hook **progress-bg gate** blocks a crew MEMBER from ending a turn with
`kind=progress` when it has **no active, non-infrastructure background subprocess** — forcing it to
instead emit `kind=question` (wait on the lead), `kind=done`, or `kind=blocked`. This catches the
"false-progress stall": a member that did some manual work, emitted `kind=progress`, and then sat
idle with nothing actually running and no signal for the lead to respond to. The gate is **Copilot-only**
today (`hooks/stop.js:1183` gates on `manifest.engine === 'copilot'`), and crews v3.6.0 explicitly
deferred the codex equivalent.

This plan ports that gate to **codex** members. A live 2026-06-09 failure (`impl-overviewdata`) had a
codex `/implement-with-ralph` member do manual scaffolding then `kind=progress`-stall with the Ralph
loop never started — exactly the stall the gate catches for Copilot, but codex was ungated. The work
is a new sibling detector (`hooks/detect-active-bg-codex.js`) that parses the codex **rollout JSONL**
transcript for backgrounded unified-exec sessions, plus a minimal-diff widening of the `hooks/stop.js`
engine gate from `copilot` to `copilot|codex`. It preserves the v3.1.0 structural-completeness and
v3.3.0 no-model-bypass invariants. Acceptance REQUIRES a LIVE codex dogfood — green unit tests are NOT
sufficient (the v3.16.0 / v3.17.0 lesson: both passed units and failed the live dogfood).

### GROUND-TRUTH codex rollout shape (verified against a REAL on-disk rollout)
Verified against `~/.codex/sessions/2026/06/05/rollout-2026-06-05T08-22-30-019e9860-…jsonl`
(155 of 1526 local rollouts carry the bg signal). Date-tree path: `~/.codex/sessions/YYYY/MM/DD/rollout-<ISO-ts>-<session-id>.jsonl`.
Every line is `{ timestamp, type, payload }`.

| Element | Shape (verified) |
|---|---|
| Turn boundary | `{ type:'event_msg', payload:{ type:'task_started' } }` |
| exec_command launch | `{ type:'response_item', payload:{ type:'function_call', name:'exec_command', call_id, arguments } }` where **`arguments` is a JSON STRING** → `JSON.parse` → `{ cmd, workdir, yield_time_ms, max_output_tokens }`. Launching cmd = `arguments.cmd`. |
| backgrounded output | `{ type:'response_item', payload:{ type:'function_call_output', call_id, output } }` where **`output` is a STRING** containing `"Process running with session ID <N>"`. (Field is `payload.output`, NOT `content`.) |
| await launch | `{ payload:{ type:'function_call', name:'await_background_completion', call_id, arguments } }` → `arguments` JSON string `{ session_id, timeout_ms, max_output_tokens }`. |
| terminal output | `{ payload:{ type:'function_call_output', call_id, output } }` where `output` contains `"Process exited with code <X>"` (or unknown-process / failure). The exit text carries **NO session id** — correlate to `N` only via the matching await's `arguments.session_id`. |

**Two corrections vs the brainstorm prose, baked into the parser spec below:** (1) the output text lives in
`payload.output` (string), and (2) `payload.arguments` is a JSON string that must be `JSON.parse`d (tolerate
parse failure → treat as unresolvable → fail toward block).

### Technical Constraints
- Codex's rollout JSONL is a different schema from Copilot's `events.jsonl`; the codex detector is a
  **separate module**, not a branch inside `detect-active-bg.js` (keeps the Copilot detector's header
  + parser intact; the two share only the infra-filter predicates and the return shape).
- Free-text parsing of codex's `core/src/tools/context.rs` output strings is version-fragile; mitigate
  with a committed real-shaped fixture and fail-toward-block on any ambiguity.
- `await_background_completion` BLOCKS the codex turn (awaits exit/timeout), so **Stop never fires while
  awaiting** ⇒ the only at-Stop bg session is launch-then-end-turn-without-await. This is what makes the
  structural-completeness argument hold for codex.

## Approach

### Architecture
A new sibling module `hooks/detect-active-bg-codex.js` exports `detectActiveBgCodex({ transcriptPath, asOf })`
returning the SAME shape as the Copilot detector (`{ activeCount, nonListenerCount, samples, asOf }`). It
parses the rollout JSONL at the Stop-supplied `transcript_path`. `hooks/stop.js` widens the engine gate to
`copilot || codex` and dispatches the codex detector by engine. The Copilot detector is untouched.

### Detector algorithm (`detectActiveBgCodex`)
Signature: `detectActiveBgCodex({ transcriptPath, asOf })` — pure on `transcriptPath`; the caller resolves the
path (see Transcript-path robustness). Steps:

1. Read the rollout JSONL at `transcriptPath` with a bounded tail read mirroring `detect-active-bg.js::readEvents`
   (a `maxEvents` budget, malformed-line tolerant). Parse each line to `{ timestamp, type, payload }`.
2. Find the **current-turn boundary**: the index of the LAST parsed line that is `type === 'event_msg'` with
   `payload.type === 'task_started'` (if none, boundary = -1, i.e. the whole window is "current turn"). "Current
   turn" = rows with index **greater than** the boundary index.
3. Single ordered walk over ALL parsed rows (correlation needs pre-boundary launches/awaits). Maintain:
   - `execLaunch: call_id → { cmd }` from each `exec_command` `function_call`. `payload.arguments` is a **JSON STRING**
     → `JSON.parse` → `cmd = parsed.cmd`. On `JSON.parse` failure, store `{ cmd: null }` (unresolvable).
   - `awaitSession: call_id → sessionId` from each `await_background_completion` `function_call`
     (`sessionId = JSON.parse(arguments).session_id`; tolerate parse failure → skip that await).
   - `sessionState: N → { lastSignal: 'running'|'terminal', lastRowIndex, cmd }`.
   For each `function_call_output` row (read `payload.output`, a STRING — NOT `content`):
   - if `/Process running with session ID (\d+)/` matches → let `N` = the captured id. Set
     `sessionState[N] = { lastSignal: 'running', lastRowIndex: <this row index> }`. Resolve `N`'s launching `cmd`:
     prefer `execLaunch[row.call_id].cmd` (an exec_command's own output); else keep any previously-recorded `cmd`
     for `N` (an `await` output re-asserting "still running" carries no exec call_id, so it refreshes liveness +
     the row index but keeps the cmd recorded at launch).
   - else if this row's `call_id ∈ awaitSession` → this is an await result that did NOT re-assert "running" for its
     session (covers `Process exited with code …`, unknown-process, failure, and timeout-without-running uniformly).
     Mark `sessionState[awaitSession[call_id]].lastSignal = 'terminal'` at this row index. **No terminal-text
     enumeration is needed** — "an await output lacking the running marker ⇒ terminal" is the structural rule.
4. **Liveness rule (biased false-NEGATIVE — the brainstorm's deliberate soundness choice)** — session `N` is
   `active-non-infra` iff ALL hold:
   a. `sessionState[N].lastSignal === 'running'` (its most recent signal is RUNNING, no later terminal); AND
   b. that signal is **CURRENT-TURN FRESH** — `lastRowIndex > boundaryIndex`. A "running" whose latest assertion
      is in a PRIOR turn (the member backgrounded in T-1 and is just spinning `progress` in T without re-touching
      it) does NOT count. **This is intentional, not a false-block bug:** the legitimate codex bg-polling idiom is
      to call `await_background_completion` this turn — which either BLOCKS the turn (so Stop never fires) or
      returns "still running" and **re-asserts the marker at a current-turn row** (re-freshening liveness via the
      step-3 refresh above). So a genuinely-polled session stays fresh; only a stale/abandoned one is blocked, and
      that false-block is recoverable (the member emits `question`/`done`/`blocked`). This deviation from Copilot's
      carry-forward is required because codex's async `ExecCommandEnd` is not guaranteed persisted to the rollout
      and restart/resume leave stale "running" lines — carrying them forward would false-PASS a dead session (the
      exact stall we fix). AND
   c. `N`'s `cmd` is resolvable AND does NOT match `isListenerArmCall(cmd) || isCrewsCliInfraCall(cmd)`. An
      unresolvable `cmd` ⇒ NOT counted as non-infra (fail toward block).
5. Return `{ activeCount, nonListenerCount, samples, asOf }`:
   - `activeCount` = count of current-turn-fresh RUNNING sessions (pre-infra-filter).
   - `nonListenerCount` = count of `active-non-infra` sessions (what the gate consumes via `computeProgressBgEffectiveActive`).
   - `samples` mirror the Copilot detector's shape for blast-radius parity:
     `{ shellId: String(sessionId), toolName: 'exec_command', command: cmd, isListener }`.
   - Do NOT emit subagent fields (out of scope). `computeProgressBgEffectiveActive` only adds `subagentActiveCount`
     when `subagentMode === 'on'`, and `Number.isFinite(undefined) === false`, so omitting them is safe.

### Failure-open / failure-toward-block contract (one explicit policy)
- `transcriptPath` resolves to **null** (no `data.transcript_path`, no `manifest.transcriptPath`, fallback found
  nothing) → the gate is **SKIPPED entirely** by the existing `if (transcriptPath)` guard (`stop.js:1190`) —
  failure-OPEN, no block.
- `transcriptPath` non-null but **unreadable / empty / all-lines-malformed** → the detector returns the empty
  result `{ activeCount: 0, nonListenerCount: 0, samples: [], asOf }` → `effectiveActive === 0` → the gate
  **BLOCKS** (failure-toward-block). This MATCHES the existing Copilot detector behavior (`detectActiveBg` returns
  `{0,0}` on an unreadable path), and the false-block is recoverable.
- The detector **throws** (unexpected) → caught by the existing `stop.js:1191-1196` try/catch → `detection = null`
  → gate **SKIPPED** (failure-open). Each of these five cases (missing path, unreadable, empty, malformed,
  fallback-miss) gets a dedicated test in US-001/US-003.

### `hooks/stop.js` gate widening (minimal diff, `:1182-1213`)
- Import the new detector at `stop.js:58` alongside `detectActiveBg`:
  `const { detectActiveBg, detectActiveBgCodex, parseSubagentMode } = require('./detect-active-bg' / './detect-active-bg-codex')`
  (the codex detector is a separate module, so add a second `require`).
- `const isCopilot = manifest.engine === 'copilot';` → add `const isCodex = manifest.engine === 'codex';`.
- Gate condition (`:1187`): replace `isCopilot` with `(isCopilot || isCodex)` AND replace `!isRetry` with
  `(isCodex || !isRetry)` — i.e. evaluate the gate even on a codex retry. (Note `(isCodex || !isRetry)` is
  logically identical to `(!isRetry || isCodex)`; the OR is commutative — the wording is chosen to read as "for
  codex, always evaluate; for Copilot, only when !isRetry". A reviewer's claim that the two orderings differ is
  incorrect.) `bumpBlockCount('progress-without-bg')` is the loop circuit breaker; for Copilot `stop_hook_active`
  is always false so the term stays inert.
- Transcript resolution (`:1189`): `const sessionId = data.session_id || manifest.sessionId || null;` and
  `const transcriptPath = data.transcript_path || manifest.transcriptPath || (isCodex ? resolveCodexTranscriptPath(sessionId) : null);`
  (only codex uses the rollout fallback; Copilot keeps its existing two-term resolution).
- Detector dispatch (inside the SAME try/catch, failure-open preserved):
  `detection = isCodex ? detectActiveBgCodex({ transcriptPath, asOf }) : detectActiveBg({ transcriptPath, asOf });`.
- Make the `:1203` log line engine-aware: `engine=${manifest.engine}`.
- **Update the gate's leading comment block** (`stop.js:~1121` and `~1155-1180`, which today document "Copilot
  only" + "isRetry skips the gate") to describe `copilot|codex` and the codex retry-evaluation behavior — leaving
  stale load-bearing guidance is a Completeness defect.
- Preserve the v3.3.0 NO-MODEL-BYPASS invariant: NO new bypass tag; only `CREWS_PROGRESS_BG_GATE=off` disables it.

### Transcript-path robustness (US-003)
`stop.js:1189` already reads `data.transcript_path || manifest.transcriptPath`. Add a codex-only last-resort
helper `resolveCodexTranscriptPath(sessionId)` (lives in `detect-active-bg-codex.js` and is exported, or a small
sibling helper) with an explicit algorithm:
1. If `sessionId` is null/empty → return null.
2. Glob `~/.codex/sessions/**/rollout-*-<sessionId>.jsonl` across the YYYY/MM/DD date-tree (the session id is the
   suffix of the rollout filename). Resolve `~` via `os.homedir()`.
3. If multiple match (restart/resume/multi-day), pick the one with the **latest embedded ISO timestamp** parsed
   from the `rollout-<ISO-ts>-<id>` filename (ties → newest `mtime`).
4. Validate the chosen file is readable and non-empty; otherwise return null.
The detector signature stays `{ transcriptPath, asOf }` — `stop.js` does the resolution and passes the result.
Failure-open contract: `resolveCodexTranscriptPath` returning null leaves `transcriptPath` null ⇒ the gate is
skipped (no block). A wrong/unreadable resolved path is impossible past the step-4 validation; if validation
mis-fires, the detector's empty-result/throw paths apply per the failure contract above. Cover the
multiple-match, no-match, and unreadable cases with tests.

### Out of Scope
- The Copilot detector internals (`detect-active-bg.js`) — unchanged.
- Codex `task`/`multi_agent` subagent fan-out counting (a separate question from unified-exec bg sessions).
  Clarification: the detector recognizes ONLY unified-exec sessions (the `Process running with session ID N`
  marker). codex subagent spawns (`spawn_agent`/`multi_agent`) are a DIFFERENT tool surface that does NOT emit
  that marker, so they are neither counted as bg work nor false-allowed — consistent with leaving subagent
  counting out of scope (and matching Copilot's opt-in `CREWS_PROGRESS_BG_SUBAGENTS` gate, which codex does not set).
- D-002 (structured manifest tracking of bg sessions via codex hooks) — needs codex-side changes; fallback only.
- The codexu root `CLAUDE.md` (gitignored — do NOT `git add`); fork guidance edits go in crews `AGENTS.md`.
- Do NOT resurrect the archived `crews-member-stalled-needs-attention-nudge`.

## Risk Areas
- **Free-text fragility**: codex's output strings could drift across releases. Mitigation: committed real-shaped
  fixture + fail-toward-block on any parse/format ambiguity. If it bites repeatedly, escalate to D-002.
- **Freshness rule is load-bearing**: a too-loose "last-signal-is-running" would false-PASS dead sessions
  (the exact stall). The current-turn-after-`task_started` scoping is the mandatory soundness correction —
  pin it with a dedicated stale-prior-turn test case.
- **`arguments` is a JSON string**: a naive `payload.arguments.cmd` (object access) silently yields `undefined`.
  Parser MUST `JSON.parse` and tolerate failure.
- **`payload.output` vs `content`**: parse the `output` field; a wrong field name silently detects nothing
  (false-PASS). Pin with the real fixture.
- **Retry bypass**: codex Stop carries `stop_hook_active`; forgetting to drop `!isRetry` for codex would let a
  blocked member re-emit progress and pass. The circuit breaker bounds the block loop so recovery stays possible.
- **Green-units-pass / dogfood-fail**: the v3.16/3.17 lesson. Acceptance is gated on a LIVE codex dogfood, not units.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A codex member emitting `kind=progress` with NO background work is BLOCKED at Stop with the canonical reason
  (`kind=progress requires active background work …`).
- A codex member with ONLY the listener (`node $env:CREWS_BIN arm`) backgrounded is BLOCKED (infra filter excludes it).
- A codex member with a **current-turn-fresh** non-infra bg session — either an `exec_command` that backgrounded
  THIS turn, OR a session re-asserted "still running" by an `await_background_completion` THIS turn — emitting
  `kind=progress` is ALLOWED.
- A codex member whose bg session was launched then exited before Stop (the await returned `Process exited with
  code` / unknown-process / failure), emitting `kind=progress`, is BLOCKED.
- A codex member whose only `Process running with session ID N` assertion is from a PRIOR turn, with no fresh
  current-turn re-touch (no exec launch and no await this turn), emitting `kind=progress`, is BLOCKED — this is the
  deliberate false-negative bias (recoverable), NOT a defect.
- The codex retry path (`stop_hook_active === true`) re-evaluates the gate (no bypass); the circuit breaker
  (`bumpBlockCount('progress-without-bg')`) bounds block loops so a blocked member can still recover.
- Failure contract holds: null/missing/fallback-miss `transcriptPath` SKIPS the gate (failure-open); a non-null but
  unreadable/empty/all-malformed transcript BLOCKS (failure-toward-block, matching Copilot); a detector throw SKIPS.
- Existing Copilot behavior is unchanged: the existing `tests/progress-bg-gate.test.js` Copilot cases stay green,
  the Copilot log line stays `engine=copilot`, the codex detector import path is NOT exercised for
  `manifest.engine === 'copilot'`, and Claude members remain skipped (gate only fires for `copilot|codex`).
- Detector unit tests pin: `payload.output` (correct field) detects while `payload.content` (wrong field) does NOT;
  `payload.arguments` JSON-string parse + parse-failure tolerance; the 5 failure-contract cases.
- A Stop e2e exercises the codex entrypoint (`hooks/codex-stop.js` → `codexToClaudeStopInput` → `handleInput` →
  `claudeDecisionToCodex`) with `stop_hook_active` round-trip, not just the shared `stop.js` handler.
- `node tests/run.js` is green (the new test file included) AND `node --check hooks/detect-active-bg-codex.js hooks/stop.js` passes.
- A LIVE codex dogfood confirms the 5-case matrix per the concrete US-005 procedure (units alone are NOT acceptance).
- 6 version stamps + `tests/version.test.js` agree on v3.21.0; `node tests/version.test.js` passes.

## Suggested Decomposition

All stories target the SAME plugin (crews). US-002 edits `hooks/stop.js` and depends on US-001's new module;
US-004 edits the shared version-stamp files + `AGENTS.md`/`CHANGELOG.md`; US-005 requires the installed plugin
(post-ship). Per the same-plugin / shared-version-file conflict rule, these CANNOT run in parallel — a single
serial cluster.

### Cluster: codex-progress-bg-gate (serial)
- Stories: US-001, US-002, US-003, US-004, US-005
- Phase: 1
- Depends on: None
- File-overlap evidence: shared=`hooks/stop.js` (US-002), version-stamp files + `AGENTS.md` + `CHANGELOG.md` (US-004); exclusive=`hooks/detect-active-bg-codex.js` (US-001), `tests/progress-bg-gate-codex.test.js` + `tests/fixtures/codex-rollout-bg.jsonl` (US-001); risk=medium (single-plugin version bump + shared stop.js edit)
- `execution_mode` rationale: Same-plugin work with a shared `hooks/stop.js` edit and shared version-stamp/changelog files forces serialization; US-002 also depends on the US-001 module and US-005 depends on a shipped+installed build. One implementer, serial.

Parallel handoff: `/implement-with-ralph --from-plan <plan_job_dir>/plan.md --parallel --suggested-decomposition <plan_job_dir>/suggested-decomposition.json`

## Open Questions
- **Version number**: this plan assumes the next minor is **v3.21.0** (current main is v3.20.0). If another
  crews ship lands first, the implementer rebases and re-derives the next free minor before bumping.
- **Live-dogfood mechanics**: the dogfood requires a real codex member spawned via crews after the version is
  shipped and `copilot plugin update` has pulled it. The implementer (or lead) drives the 5-case matrix; cases
  (1)/(2)/(4)/(5) are BLOCK, case (3) is ALLOW. A committed dogfood transcript/record under
  `.ralph/jobs/<job>/dogfood/` is the evidence artifact.
- **Fixture provenance**: `tests/fixtures/codex-rollout-bg.jsonl` should be a redacted slice of a REAL rollout
  (a real example exists at `~/.codex/sessions/2026/06/05/rollout-…019e9860…jsonl`); redact absolute paths/PII but
  keep the exact line shapes (`payload.output` strings, JSON-string `payload.arguments`, the `task_started` boundary).

<summary>Phase 4 multi-model plan review (Claude sonnet-4.5 + Codex gpt-5.x + Copilot) — 14 findings, all resolved</summary>

Three reviewers ran in parallel against the draft. Consensus drove the revisions; see
`plan-review-findings.json` for the full manifest. Adopted: thread `sessionId` into the codex transcript
resolution (F-001); Copilot-parity `samples` shape `{shellId,toolName,command,isListener}` (F-002); structural
terminal rule "an await output lacking the running marker ⇒ terminal" (F-003); explicit five-case failure
contract (F-005); update the stale Copilot-only / isRetry-skip comment block in `stop.js` (F-007); codex-stop.js
round-trip e2e (F-008); `payload.output`-vs-`content` assertion (F-009); concrete lead-owned post-merge dogfood
procedure (F-010, F-013); rephrased "byte-identical" criterion (F-011); single-walk `sessionState` clarification
(F-014); subagent-surface clarification (F-012). Clarified-and-defended (NOT weakened): the current-turn
freshness rule (F-004) — the apparent contradiction with structural-completeness is resolved by the await-refresh
path (a legitimately-polled session is re-asserted "still running" by a current-turn `await_background_completion`,
so it stays fresh; only a stale/abandoned prior-turn session is blocked, recoverably). Rejected as stated:
`(isCodex || !isRetry)` ≡ `(!isRetry || isCodex)` — the OR is commutative (F-006, downgraded to Low).

</details>
